text.title: User Story Mapping Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding User Story Mapping. Each pairs a binary check with a sourced rationale; HARD rules — user-supplied input cannot override.

rule.statement: Build the activity backbone (left-to-right journey) before writing any story. The backbone is 5-10 verb phrases ("Create Project"), never nouns ("Project"). Read it aloud as a user narrative before continuing.
rule.rationale: Noun backbones hide the actions and quietly turn the map back into a feature list. Fewer than 5 activities means the journey is not yet decomposed; more than 10 means two maps were merged. Reading aloud is the cheapest test that the row is a narrative rather than a taxonomy.

rule.statement: First horizontal slice is the walking skeleton — the minimum end-to-end journey that works, with exactly one task per backbone activity, each end-to-end completeable.
rule.rationale: One-task-per-activity is what makes the skeleton machine-checkable and what forces it to span the journey. A skeleton that covers only the favourite activities ships a Release 1 with mid-journey gaps.

rule.statement: Per task, the vertical column lists alternative stories ranked top = MVP, capped at 6 per column.
rule.rationale: Ranking is what turns the column into a decision; an unranked column is a wish list. Past six the column stops being scannable in a workshop and the ranking becomes noise.

rule.statement: Scope cuts are made by drawing horizontal slice lines, not deleting stories.
rule.rationale: A deleted story is an invisible decision; a story below the line is a decision a stakeholder can see, argue with, and reverse. Visible scope-cutting is the whole reason the map exists.

rule.statement: One persona per map; multiple personas → multiple maps.
rule.rationale: With three personas on one map the vertical alternatives become incomparable and a horizontal slice stops meaning anything — it is no longer one coherent release for one user.

rule.statement: Every activity carries at least one error-path or empty-state task — not just the happy path.

rationale.source: Jeff Patton Story Mapping; practitioner experience

rule.rationale: Error and empty states feel like "edge cases" during mapping and then consume a third of the build. Forcing one per activity puts that work on the map where it can be sliced, instead of discovering it mid-release.

rule.statement: Every release slice spans the full backbone. A slice covering only some activities is rejected.
rule.rationale: A release covering 2 of 5 activities ships a broken journey: the user can start but not finish. Full-backbone slices are what make each release independently usable.

rule.statement: If preconditions in AGENTS.md "Applies If" do not all hold, OR any "Skip If" disqualifier is true, do not run this methodology — route to the named alternative.
rule.rationale: Methodologies are pre-condition gated; running them out-of-scope produces noise and burns the agent context budget.

rule.statement: If preconditions hold, execute the procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml` (or the rule set above when complexity is light), emit the artefact specified by `content/02-output-contract.xml`, and validate with `scripts/validate-user-story-mapping.py` before returning.
rule.rationale: Tying the entry rule to the validator script closes the loop between policy and machine check.
